overall_verdict.model_artifacts: All six are acceptable bounded receipt interpretations.
overall_verdict.A_controls: Failed: vitals-before-open is accepted, and injected close9 is concealed by a successful producer result without retained diagnostics.
overall_verdict.B_controls: The supplied ordering rejection, cleanup-failure propagation and diagnostic-retention controls pass. The injected close9 run itself remains failed.
overall_verdict.claim_ceiling: No full Browser workflow acceptance, real-browser crash recovery, application acceptance, superiority or relative cost/benefit conclusion.

checks: Request and all three shared historical input hashes match the packet.
Both cleanup and both ordering receipt hashes match the packet.
All ten frozen Browser source-file pins match intake.
All six artifact and trace hashes match their receipts.
All six receipts equal their trial-index entries.
All six session start/final timestamps and recorded model metadata agree with existing session records.
All event timestamps fall within their trial intervals.
All six elapsed intervals match timestamp arithmetic and are below 300 seconds.
Observed trial order is A1, B1, B2, A2, A3, B3, without overlapping trial intervals.
Every original tool output exactly matches the complete concatenation of its named current frozen/input files; no original output truncation was found.
Observed calls are file reads only, confined to assigned-arm frozen Skill/references and named shared/arm inputs.
No opposite-arm, prior-trial or reviewer-output reads appear in original traces.
limitations: Recorded metadata is not authenticated serving identity.
Observed read-only compliance is not enforced filesystem isolation.
Durable saving is parent-mediated, not autonomous model saving.
Six interpretations reuse parent-produced evidence; they are not six independent browser executions.
Reviewer display truncation occurred during broad reads and was resolved using bounded reads and exact-content comparisons; this is separate from original trial outputs.

ordering.interpretation: Supplying a route on vitals does not establish an initial open. These receipts exercise actual plan validation, not browser execution.

cleanup.disposition: Compatible with successful fake-browser cleanup, but independent cleanup-result reporting is absent.
Failed control: injected cleanup failure is not propagated or retained.
Failed run; passed failure-propagation and diagnostic-retention control. Recovery remains unexecuted.

ground_truth.conformance_boundary: All four fixtures report passing positive controls and zero prohibited-origin hits. Negative actions return exit1 with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT. The fake executable synthesizes these responses without real browser enforcement; zero hits cannot establish request-time browser protection. Frame coverage is combined with initial-open-and-frame, not a separately executed named negative case.

archive_contents.conformance-result.json: Parsed archive is exactly equal to the complete B close9 stdout result, including all nine cases, failed cleanup and recovery facts.

recovery_facts.suggestion: retry isolated close, then remove private diagnostics

retention_boundary: B close9 retained its private root at producer completion.
Parent archived JSON before removing the owned outer fixture root.
The fixture cleanup receipt reports removal; both outer root and B recovery root are currently absent.
Archived JSON remains readable evidence. The original recovery path is not a currently available recovery environment.
Directory removal does not establish successful browser-session recovery.

historical_actual_browser.provenance: Shared historical parent-operated, B-produced execution on a caller-owned synthetic loopback page; not an A producer run or fresh execution by any original model trial.
historical_actual_browser.raw_evidence_boundary: Six historical private raw-output pointers are retained in the run receipt. All six pointed-to files are currently absent, consistent with recorded scratch cleanup. Their raw contents cannot be independently reinspected from these pointers.
missing_details: Detailed historical prepare/probe and executable-identity evidence
historical_actual_browser.interpretation: Supports the six recorded synthetic-page actions and separate cleanup outcome. It neither repairs A's failed controls nor establishes application acceptance.

common_contract: SKILL.md and route-and-report.md are byte-identical across A/B.
Workflow owns route mapping, semantic effect authorization and claim adequacy.
Wrapper owns deterministic plan shape/order, private context, subprocess boundaries and isolated browser cleanup.
Page observations cannot authorize commands or effects.
A_failure_mechanisms: vitals is allowed but absent from PAGE_CONTEXT_ACTIONS, so its placement before the first open escapes the ordering gate.
Conformance finally invokes close but discards its result.
A unconditionally removes the private conformance root before constructing its reported result.
A's success calculation omits close outcome, matching the supplied close9 false-success receipt.
B_mechanisms: Adds vitals to PAGE_CONTEXT_ACTIONS; validateTestPlan rejects it before first open with step_index and reason_code.
Captures close as an independent cleanup result.
Requires passed cleanup in the producer's overall success calculation.
Retains failed-run diagnostics and writes conformance-result.json with private file permissions.
Wrapper conformance consumption independently requires cleanup passed, exit0, no timeout and no error.
Failed producer results can expose a bounded private recovery evidence reference.
Pipeline reference explicitly documents vitals ordering and cleanup blockers.
producer_limits: Parent prepare-browser-cleanup.py deliberately creates a fake executable, injects close exit0/exit9 and archives retained JSON before removing scratch.
This exercises conformance-producer behavior; it does not demonstrate a real browser close failure.

Parent prepare-browser.py is a separate lifecycle producer using direct agent-browser calls and an allowed-domain setting. Its source is not proof of the unique wrapper's exact-origin enforcement, and its lifecycle outputs are not substituted for the named CEOPT-29 inputs.
The inspected mechanisms are not promoted into unexecuted runtime facets.
Other wrapper action-policy differences exist in the frozen source; these supplied cases do not validate every added action alias or interaction path.
